h1: Rio de Janeiro travel, stays & events guide
heroText: Rio de Janeiro is Brazil's beach-and-mountain icon, where city life wraps around Guanabara Bay, forested peaks and long Atlantic beaches. Ride up to Christ the Redeemer, take the cable car to Sugarloaf Mountain, then choose between Copacabana Beach and Ipanema Beach for daily rhythm. Galeao handles long-haul flights, while Santos Dumont is handy for domestic hops.

areas.name: Ipanema
areas.text: Ipanema is the best all-round first base, with beach life, restaurants, metro access and safer evening movement than many central areas.

areas.name: Copacabana
areas.text: Copacabana has the deepest hotel supply and famous beachfront, useful for value, tours and classic Rio atmosphere.

areas.name: Leblon
areas.text: Leblon is upscale and calmer, with excellent restaurants, beach access and a polished base beside Ipanema.

areas.name: Botafogo
areas.text: Botafogo gives easier access to Sugarloaf, metro routes and bay views, often at better prices than the beach districts.

areas.name: Santa Teresa
areas.text: Santa Teresa is atmospheric and hillside, best for boutique stays, art, views and travelers comfortable using taxis at night.

airports.name: Rio de Janeiro Galeao International Airport (GIG)
airports.search: Rio de Janeiro Galeao International Airport, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
airports.text: Galeao is Rio's main international airport on Ilha do Governador; allow extra time between the airport and South Zone beaches.

airports.name: Santos Dumont Airport (SDU)
airports.search: Santos Dumont Airport, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
airports.text: Santos Dumont is close to downtown and the bay, convenient for many domestic flights and short transfers.

airportTransfer.value: 30-60 min by taxi or ride-hail to Centro, longer to the beach zones in traffic
airportTransfer.note: from Rio de Janeiro Galeao International Airport
airportTransfer.distance: about 20 km north of central Rio

stayOverview: Choose Ipanema for the easiest first Rio stay, Copacabana for hotel choice and classic beachfront value, or Leblon for a calmer upscale base. Botafogo is practical for metro and Sugarloaf, while Santa Teresa suits boutique stays with taxi use.
hotelIntro: Rio hotel choice should balance beach access, evening safety and airport transfers: Ipanema is the strongest default, Copacabana gives range, Leblon is polished, Botafogo is practical, and Santa Teresa is scenic but less simple late at night.
rentalCars: Skip a rental car in Rio; traffic, parking and security make metro, taxis, rideshare and tours easier.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Stay in Ipanema or Leblon for a first visit if beach days, restaurants and easier evening movement matter most.

travelTips.title: Airport timing
travelTips.text: Leave generous time for Galeao transfers, especially before international flights or when crossing town in weekday traffic.

travelTips.title: Safety basics
travelTips.text: Keep phones discreet on beaches and busy streets, use taxis or rideshare late, and avoid isolated viewpoints after dark.

travelTips.title: Weather buffer
travelTips.text: Book Christ the Redeemer and Sugarloaf with some flexibility because cloud can hide the views even on warm days.

nearbyIdeas.name: Niteroi
nearbyIdeas.label: Bay
nearbyIdeas.text: Niteroi is a quick bay crossing for Oscar Niemeyer architecture, beaches and views back toward Rio's skyline.

nearbyIdeas.name: Petropolis
nearbyIdeas.label: Heritage
nearbyIdeas.text: Petropolis offers imperial history and cooler mountain air, making it one of Rio's classic day trips.

nearbyIdeas.name: Ilha Grande
nearbyIdeas.label: Island
nearbyIdeas.text: Ilha Grande is better as an overnight beach escape, with boat transfers, trails and car-free village stays.
